title: Surge-resilient routing coordinator and dependency modernization
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary:
We will refactor the smart routing control path to introduce a surge-resilient coordinator that decouples policy evaluation from fallback execution and reduces dependency surface area on legacy routing shims. This ticket combines targeted code cleanup, dependency upgrades (protobuf, metrics client), and an end-to-end performance pass to reduce tail latency under bursty load.

Goals:
- Replace synchronous policy evaluator call sites with an evented coordinator that processes policy decisions off the hot request path.
- Implement a compact, lock-free fallback queue for short-circuiting overloaded regional routes.
- Upgrade protobuf schema lib to 3.22.x and internal metrics-client to v1.9 to unlock batching telemetry and avoid an OOM bug under heavy tracing.
- Reduce median and p95 routing decision latency by 25% and 40% respectively in CI workload replay.
- Provide clear rollout and rollback plan, with feature flags to enable coordinator per-route.

Scope / Non-goals:
In-scope: core smart-router package, policy-evaluator adapter, fallback worker, unit/e2e tests, CI benchmarks, lightweight console telemetry hooks.
Out-of-scope: full regional-lease protocol rewrite, dedicated autoscaler changes, and downstream client-side SDKs. Those will be separate follow-ups.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Evented coordinator model: trades slightly higher avg allocations for elimination of synchronous lock contention on the hot path. Chosen because previous analysis showed lock contention drove p99 spikes during bursts.
- Fallback queue is length-bounded per-region to avoid head-of-line blocking; we use an eviction policy that prefers dropping low-priority background requests before critical customer traffic.
- We keep the existing route-selector deterministic for now; a future ticket will explore probabilistic fast-paths.
- Upgrading protobuf requires a small wire-compatible schema migration; we will keep backward compatibility via adapter functions and a compatibility test in CI.

Migration and rollout plan:
1) Merge coordinator with feature flag off; run canary benchmark in staging replay (2026-03-15).
2) Enable feature flag for small region shard with internal traffic (2026-03-18).
3) Monitor key metrics for 24h: routing_latency_{median,p95,p99}, fallback_rate, route_error_rate, OOM counts.
4) Gradual ramp to 50% then 100% with rollback if any safety thresholds tripped.

Testing and metrics:
- Unit tests for coordinator state transitions and fallback eviction logic.
- Integration test that replays production trace sample and asserts latency and fallback stability.
- Bench harness to measure p50/p95/p99 for policy evaluation under varying QPS and request size distributions.
- Dashboard: routing-coordinator.v2 in Console (temporary tile) showing latency heatmaps, queue lengths, and eviction counts.

Acceptance criteria (see field):
- Coordinator enabled behind feature flag and passing staging benchmarks that show >=25% p95 improvement vs baseline.
- No regression in correctness tests (route selection, regional affinity) and rollout runbook verified.
- Protobuf and metrics-client upgrades merged, green in CI, and no regressions in schema compatibility tests.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: subtle ordering bugs causing wrong fallback target selection. Mitigation: exhaustive unit tests + e2e trace replays + canary on low-impact shard.
- Risk: upgrade exposes new GC pressure. Mitigation: run long-running soak in staging and monitor memory; revert if OOMs increase beyond threshold.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Surge-Resilient+Routing+Coordinator
- Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/smart-router/pull/1287
- Bench results (staging run 2026-03-10): https://internal.redwood.ai/bench/routing-coordinator/2026-03-10
